en: Although invisible, air is a mixture of gases that takes up space and has measurable mass.
When a puddle dries, the liquid water does not disappear but changes into an invisible gas that still exists.
Melting a chocolate bar is a physical change because it only changes state and forms no new substance.
Rusting iron is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen to form a completely new substance.
Dissolved sugar does not vanish; it breaks into invisible particles that remain in the water and add mass.
Boiling water is a physical change because the bubbling steam is still made of the exact same water molecules.
Liquids have different viscosities, meaning thick honey flows much slower than thin water due to internal friction.
Burning wood does not destroy matter, as the original mass is conserved in the remaining ash and released gases.
Brass is a solid solution of copper and zinc, proving that solutions can exist in the solid state.
Cutting a piece of paper in half changes its shape, but the total amount of matter remains constant.
A helium balloon floats due to buoyancy, but the helium gas inside still possesses a definite, measurable mass.
Though they expand to fill their container, gas particles like oxygen still take up space and possess volume.
